citation.title: AutoMS: Multi-Agent Evolutionary Search for Cross-Physics Inverse Microstructure Design
citation.authors: Zhenyuan Zhao; Yu Xing; Tianyang Xue; Lingxin Cao; Xin Yan; Lin Lu

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across 17 cross-physics design tasks, AutoMS reports an 83.8% success rate and better task completion than traditional evolutionary optimization baselines.
claim.key_phrase: 83.8% success rate on 17 diverse cross-physics tasks
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML speed-up is reported; the 23.3% runtime reduction in Sec. 1 is against the ML ReAct baseline.
claim.alternatives: Sec. 1 reports 23.3% lower wall-clock time than ReAct (an agentic baseline), which is not a classical comparator.

baseline.classical_method: NSGA-II, Bayesian optimization, and CMA-ES for inverse microstructure design (Table 1)
baseline.implementation: AutoMS multi-agent LLM framework; numerical baseline implementation details not stated
baseline.solver: Preconditioned conjugate gradient for homogenization simulations (Appendix D); optimizer baseline solver details not stated
baseline.problem_size: 17 tasks; periodic RVE simulation at 64^3 voxels (Appendix D)
baseline.classical_time: not stated for classical methods; AutoMS mean wall-clock 2180.5 s per task over four runs (Table 8 / Appendix C.5)
baseline.ml_time: 2180.5 s mean per task (four runs; Appendix C.3/Table 8)
baseline.training_time: not stated; uses pre-trained MIND generator
baseline.quality_metric: success rate, constraint satisfaction rate, mean relative error, best property match, and quality score (Appendix E)
baseline.quality_gap: AutoMS success rate 83.8% versus NSGA-II 43.7%, Bayesian optimization 65.0%, and CMA-ES 66.7% (Table 1).

R1.evidence: Abstract's primary comparison concerns task success and property matching; it does not compare speed at matched design quality or time.

R2.evidence: Table 1 compares success rates rather than classical runtimes; no classical per-iteration timing is given.

R3.evidence: The primary outcome is design success; the separate runtime comparison in Sec. 1 is against ReAct, not a classical method.

R4.evidence: Appendix D describes homogenization and plasticity simulations used to evaluate generated structures; Sec. 5.4 analyzes failures and reports an 83.8% success rate across benchmark tasks.

notes: The abstract's quantitative comparison is task success/property quality against classical evolutionary algorithms, so this is the quality stratum. The distinct efficiency claim compares AutoMS with ReAct only. Table 8 reports four independent runs; Sec. 5.4 analyzes failures, and the 16.2% failure rate is the complement of the reported 83.8% success rate.
